items.name: Squat to Overhead Reach
items.description: A bodyweight squat finished with a long overhead reach, linking the legs, hips and upper back in one smooth movement.
items.setup: Stand with feet about shoulder-width apart, toes turned out slightly, and arms by your sides.
steps: Sit your hips back and down into a comfortable squat, reaching your arms forward for balance.
Keep your chest lifted and your knees in line with your toes.
Press through your whole foot to stand up.
As you straighten, sweep both arms overhead and reach tall before lowering them.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you lower and out as you stand and reach.
mistakes: Lifting the heels off the floor.
Arching the lower back during the overhead reach.
items.easier: Squat down to a chair seat behind you and reach only to shoulder height.
items.harder: Pause for two seconds at the bottom of each squat.
cautions: Squat only as deep as you can with your heels down and without knee pain.

items.name: Burpee
items.description: A demanding full-body move that combines a squat, a plank, a push-up and a jump.
items.setup: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart in a space with room for a plank and a jump. A non-slip floor is important.
steps: Squat down and place your hands on the floor just in front of your feet.
Jump or step both feet back into a high plank.
Lower your chest to the floor for a push-up, then press back up.
Jump or step your feet back toward your hands.
Stand and jump up, reaching your arms overhead, then land softly.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you push up and as you jump; breathe in on the way down.
mistakes: Letting the hips sag when landing in the plank.
Rushing so much that technique falls apart.
items.easier: Use the Step-Back Burpee: step the feet back and forward, and skip the push-up and the jump.
items.harder: Add a tuck jump at the top while keeping every landing soft and controlled.
cautions: High impact: choose the step-back version if jumping bothers your joints.
Stop and rest if you feel dizzy or lightheaded.

items.name: Step-Back Burpee
items.description: A no-jump version of the burpee that still works the legs, core and shoulders while keeping impact low.
items.setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart with clear floor space in front of you.
steps: Squat down and place your hands flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
Step one foot back, then the other, into a high plank.
Hold the plank for a moment with your body in a straight line.
Step your feet back toward your hands one at a time.
Stand up tall and reach your arms overhead.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you stand and reach, and keep breathing while in the plank.
mistakes: Dropping the hips or lifting them high in the plank.
Rounding the back heavily when placing the hands down.
items.easier: Place your hands on a sturdy chair seat or step instead of the floor.
items.harder: Add a push-up in the plank, or progress to the full Burpee.
cautions: Keep your wrists under your shoulders, and use fists if your wrists are uncomfortable.

items.name: Bear Plank Hold
items.description: A hovering hands-and-knees hold that builds core and shoulder stability in very little space.
items.setup: Start on hands and knees with hands under shoulders and knees under hips. Tuck your toes under.
steps: Brace your core as if preparing for a gentle poke to the stomach.
Lift your knees about 2 to 5 cm (1 to 2 inches) off the floor.
Keep your back flat and your head in line with your spine.
Hold steady while breathing, then lower your knees gently.
items.breathing: Take slow, controlled breaths throughout the hold.
mistakes: Lifting the hips high instead of hovering the knees.
Letting the back round or sag.
items.easier: Hold for shorter periods, lowering the knees to rest whenever you need to.
items.harder: Lift one hand off the floor at a time without letting the hips shift.
cautions: Use fists, or rest on your forearms, if your wrists are uncomfortable.

items.name: Plank to Downward Dog
items.description: Flows between a high plank and a downward-dog shape to work the shoulders and core while lengthening the backs of the legs.
items.setup: Begin in a high plank with hands under shoulders and feet hip-width apart.
steps: Brace your core so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Push the floor away and lift your hips up and back into an upside-down V.
Let your head relax between your arms and ease your heels toward the floor.
Shift your weight forward and lower your hips back to the plank.
items.breathing: Breathe out as you lift into the V and in as you return to the plank.
mistakes: Rushing so the hips sag in the plank.
Locking the knees hard in the V shape.
items.easier: Perform the movement from your knees, or keep the knees softly bent in the V.
items.harder: Add a push-up each time you return to the plank.
cautions: Rise slowly afterwards if head-down positions make you dizzy.
Use fists if your wrists are uncomfortable.

items.name: Dumbbell Thruster
items.description: A front squat that flows into an overhead press, working most major muscle groups in one movement.
items.setup: Hold a pair of light dumbbells at your shoulders, palms facing each other, with feet shoulder-width apart.
steps: Brace your core and squat down until your thighs are about parallel to the floor, or as low as is comfortable.
Drive up through your feet to stand.
Use the momentum from standing to press the dumbbells straight overhead.
Lower the weights back to your shoulders with control before the next squat.
items.breathing: Breathe in as you squat down and out as you stand and press.
mistakes: Letting the elbows drop forward during the squat.
Arching the lower back at the top of the press.
Choosing weights that are too heavy to control overhead.
items.easier: Separate the two moves – squat, then press – with a pause in between, or use lighter weights.
items.harder: Use slightly heavier weights, or slow the lowering phase to three seconds.
cautions: Make sure you have clear space overhead.
Skip the press if overhead movement causes shoulder pain.
